cause: The 2.2.18 product read a sealed command spool changed after its seal and ran it: DesktopControlDocuments.consume read through ControlTransferStore.acquire/Consumer.read, which return the spool's current bytes, and DesktopControlTransferSpool.sha256() is the running digest of the appended bytes, so the seal's digest was never compared with what was read. The harness's same-length control-snapshot naming a foreign controller reached DesktopHeadlessSession, which refused it: cli-response\terror\t1\tCONFLICT, the 37-byte frame (sha256 cc0f2ba7c0b358866473b781264fc7e7a02ae48be340c52204e4e51e1f4e6c5d). The harness then kept its writer, payload and spool-folder handles after that finished exchange, so the CLI cases' close_known refused and the owner parked its clone.
execution: Only module definitions run. The owner runs with the inert guest of test_windows_cli_native_failures and test_windows_document_acceptance; mutate_sealed_spool and the client run for real over a socket pair whose far end is a logical product owner writing a real temporary spool file. No process, listener, Win32 call or VM is involved.

document-client-negative.before.source.defect: Client.negative raised document-negative-admitted without the reply it had decoded, so nothing could name what the product answered.

document-native-spool.before.source.defect: mutate_sealed_spool kept its writer, payload and spool-folder handles after the product answered the honest reference of the changed spool, a finished exchange, so the row parked instead of closing as its named known failure.
